name: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)
summary: A 5-year, multiple-entry visa for remote workers, digital nomads and freelancers working for clients or employers outside Thailand, and for people coming to do a 'Thai soft power' activity such as Muay Thai training, a Thai cooking course or medical treatment. Each entry gives you up to 180 days, and you can extend once per entry for another 180 days. The fee is 10,000 THB (paid in local currency) and you need to show at least 500,000 THB in savings. From 31 August 2026 you also need a police clearance certificate and proof of permanent residence in the country where you apply.
seoTitle: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) 2026: remote work & Muay Thai visa guide
seoDescription: DTV explained: 5 years, 180 days per entry plus 180-day extension, 10,000 THB fee, 500,000 THB funds, new police-clearance and residence rules, and documents for remote workers and Muay Thai students.
validity: 5 years from issue, multiple entries. Each entry allows a stay of up to 180 days.
extendableDetail: Once per entry, you can extend your stay by up to another 180 days at an immigration office in Thailand, so up to 360 days in a row. After that you must leave Thailand; when you come back you get a fresh 180 days while the visa is still valid.
feeNote: 10,000 THB, charged in the currency of the embassy that processes your e-Visa (for example GBP 300 in London, USD 400 in Washington, EUR 350 in Helsinki). Non-refundable, even if refused. Extensions at immigration are paid separately.
financialRequirement: At least 500,000 THB (or the equivalent in your currency) in a bank account in your name. Embassies differ on how long it must have been there: some accept a recent ending balance, others (such as Washington) want 3 months of statements showing the amount throughout. Funds deposited just before applying are a common reason for refusal.
processingTime: Varies by embassy, usually 1 to 3 weeks once the application is complete. Allow at least a month, and longer if you still need a police clearance certificate.
keyRequirements: Aged 20 or over (spouses and children under 20 of a DTV holder can apply as dependants)
At least 500,000 THB in savings in your own name
Workcation: remote work or freelancing for employers or clients outside Thailand
Soft power: enrolment in a qualifying activity, such as Muay Thai, a Thai cooking course, sports training or medical treatment
Since 31 August 2026: a police clearance certificate from your country of nationality or residence
Since 31 August 2026: proof of permanent residence in the country where you apply, and you must apply through the embassy covering that country
No work for Thai employers or Thai clients
documents: Passport valid for at least 6 months, plus a recent photo
Bank statements in your name showing at least 500,000 THB (period depends on the embassy)
Police clearance certificate (criminal record check), issued recently; London wants it within 6 months, Washington within 3 months
Proof of permanent residence where you apply (national ID, residence permit, green card or similar)
Workcation: employment contract or letter from your foreign employer, or for freelancers a portfolio, client contracts and invoices, and company registration if you run a business

Soft power: a letter of acceptance or enrolment from the Muay Thai camp, cooking school or other provider, with course dates, plus proof you have paid (receipts); for medical treatment, a hospital appointment letter
Dependants: marriage or birth certificate and a copy of the main applicant's DTV and passport
Proof of accommodation for at least your first days in Thailand (some embassies ask for a minimum 7-night booking)
Certified English translations of any documents in another language

howToApply.detail: Workcation if you'll work remotely for foreign clients or an employer; soft power if you're coming to train Muay Thai, take a cooking course, get medical treatment or join a similar activity; dependant if your spouse or parent holds a DTV.

howToApply.step: Get your police clearance and funds ready
howToApply.detail: Order a criminal record check from your home country early; it can take weeks. Make sure 500,000 THB has been sitting in your account for as long as your embassy asks.

howToApply.step: For soft power: book your activity
howToApply.detail: Enrol with a registered Thai provider, such as a Muay Thai camp, and ask for an official acceptance letter on letterhead with your name, passport number, course length and dates. Pay at least the first part of the fees and keep the receipt.
Apply through the embassy that covers the country where you are a citizen or permanent resident. Choose 'Destination Thailand Visa', upload all documents and pay the fee.
Submit the TDAC within 3 days before arrival. You'll be stamped in for 180 days.
Before your 180 days run out, either extend once for another 180 days at immigration or leave and come back for a fresh 180-day stay.

bestFor: Digital nomads and remote employees working for companies outside Thailand
Muay Thai students training for months at a Thai camp
People doing Thai cooking courses, Thai massage courses or other longer cultural programmes
Travellers wanting several long stays over five years
notFor: Working for a Thai company or Thai clients (you need a Non-Immigrant B visa and a work permit)
Anyone who can't get a clean police clearance certificate
Applicants hoping to apply from a third country they're only visiting
commonMistakes: Depositing the 500,000 THB just before applying. Embassies want to see the money held over time.
Vague freelance evidence. A single invoice or a LinkedIn profile is not enough; show contracts, invoices and a portfolio.
Using a Muay Thai camp or school that isn't a registered business, or a letter without dates and course length.
Applying at an embassy in a country where you're a tourist. Since 31 August 2026 you must apply where you hold citizenship or permanent residence.
Forgetting the police clearance certificate, now required for all applicants.
Taking on Thai clients or local jobs. The DTV only covers work for foreign employers or clients.
Assuming 180 days per year. It's 180 days per entry, and the clock restarts each time you enter.

faqs.q: How much money do I need for the DTV?
faqs.a: At least 500,000 THB (or equivalent) in a bank account in your name. How long it must be held depends on the embassy: some only look at the ending balance, others want 3 months of statements. If you're sponsored, some embassies accept a sponsorship letter; ask yours.

faqs.q: Can I get a DTV to train Muay Thai?
faqs.a: Yes. Muay Thai is one of the headline soft-power activities. You'll need an acceptance letter from a registered Muay Thai camp with your course dates, proof you've paid, and the same 500,000 THB funds, police clearance and residence proof as every applicant.

faqs.q: Can I do a Thai massage or cooking course on a DTV?
faqs.a: Thai cooking courses are explicitly listed. Thai massage and wellness courses at established schools are commonly accepted as soft-power activities, but embassies decide case by case, so check with yours before paying for a long course.

faqs.q: How long can I stay on a DTV?
faqs.a: Up to 180 days per entry, and you can extend once per entry for another 180 days at immigration. The visa is valid for 5 years, so you can repeat this pattern as long as the visa hasn't expired.
Yes. Your spouse and children under 20 can apply for a dependant DTV. They need proof of the relationship, such as a marriage or birth certificate, and a copy of your DTV details.

faqs.q: Do I pay Thai tax on a DTV?
faqs.a: The visa doesn't change tax rules. If you spend 180 days or more in Thailand in a calendar year you may become a Thai tax resident, and foreign income brought into Thailand can then be taxable. Speak to a tax adviser.

faqs.q: What changed for the DTV on 31 August 2026?
faqs.a: Three things: every applicant must include a police clearance certificate, you must prove permanent residence in the country where you apply, and you can only apply through the embassy covering your country of citizenship or legal residence. Applications filed before 31 August 2026 are processed under the old rules.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the DTV while I'm in Thailand?
faqs.a: Generally no. Under the 2026 rules you apply through the Thai embassy covering your country of citizenship or permanent residence, via the e-Visa system, not from inside Thailand.
